entities.evidence: Genesis 11:27 identifies Lot as Haran’s son and Abram’s nephew. Here he travels with Abram and owns the flocks, herds, and tents.
Abram is Terah’s son and Lot’s uncle, later named Abraham. Here he is Lot’s traveling companion.

name_review_base.evidence: Genesis 11:27 identifies Lot as Haran’s son and Abram’s nephew. Here he travels with Abram and owns the flocks, herds, and tents.
Abram is Terah’s son and Lot’s uncle, later named Abraham. Here he is Lot’s traveling companion.

analysis.evidence: וְגַם לְלוֹט means “and Lot too.” The verse adds Lot, who traveled with Abram, as another possessor of flocks, cattle, and tents.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The additive particle גַם means “also” and places the focus on לְלוֹט.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לוֹט. Its etymology is uncertain.
draft.definition: Lot, son of Haran and nephew of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 names Lot as Haran’s son and Abram as Haran’s brother. Genesis 13:5 names Lot as the owner of the livestock and tents.

analysis.evidence: הַהֹלֵךְ אֶת אַבְרָם identifies Lot as the man traveling with Abram. With וְגַם and הָיָה, the clause reads “Lot also had flocks, cattle, and tents.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לְ marks the possessor in a clause with הָיָה. Its complement is the personal name לוֹט.

analysis.evidence: In הַהֹלֵךְ אֶת אַבְרָם, אֶת means “with” and identifies Abram as Lot’s traveling companion.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, describing Lot.

analysis.evidence: הַהֹלֵךְ אֶת אַבְרָם describes Lot as traveling with Abram. אֶת introduces אַבְרָם as Lot’s companion. The source gloss “with you (plural)” would require a pronominal suffix.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: הַהֹלֵךְ אֶת אַבְרָם describes Lot as traveling with Abram. אַבְרָם names Lot’s companion.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: The fronted phrase לְלוֹט identifies Lot as the possessor. The nouns following הָיָה list what he had: flocks, cattle, and tents.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: לְלוֹט … הָיָה introduces Lot’s possessions. The list pairs צֹאן with בָקָר ‘cattle’ and then adds אֹהָלִים ‘tents’, identifying צֹאן as his sheep and goats.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders, singular absolute, with collective meaning.
analysis.sense: flock, sheep and goats, as livestock

analysis.evidence: The verse lists Lot’s possessions. וּבָקָר follows צֹאן “flocks” and precedes וְאֹהָלִים “and tents,” identifying cattle as a group.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” בָקָר is a common noun of both genders, singular in the absolute state, with collective meaning.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists what Lot owned. וְאֹהָלִים adds tents to his flocks and cattle.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ ‘and’ prefixes אֹהָלִים, the masculine plural absolute of אֹהֶל.
